conventions: Formatting is Prettier 2.6 with @excalidraw/prettier-config: 2-space indent, double quotes, semicolons, trailing commas everywhere ("all"), 80-column print width, Markdown proseWrap never.

ESLint import/order: groups builtin, external (with @excalidraw/** placed after other externals), internal, parent, sibling, index, then type imports last; a blank line between groups is allowed and used as in the surrounding file.
Type-only imports are separate `import type { ... } from "...";` statements (@typescript-eslint/consistent-type-imports, separate-type-imports style).
Every if/else body uses braces (curly); no console.log; no unused variables; prefer optional chaining and ?? over manual null checks.
TypeScript strict: no `any`, no `@ts-ignore`/`@ts-expect-error`, no eslint-disable comments, no non-null assertions on values that can be undefined.

Internal packages are imported by their package names (`@excalidraw/math`, `@excalidraw/element`, `@excalidraw/common`); types from `@excalidraw/math/types` and `@excalidraw/element/types`; editor types from `../types`.

Tests use Vitest globals (describe, it, beforeEach, expect without importing them) and the repo helpers: `render`/`act`/`assertSelectedElements` from ./test-utils, `API` from ./helpers/api, `Pointer`/`Keyboard` from ./helpers/ui; `const { h } = window;` gives the app handle.
Change only the lines a site names; every other line of an edited file stays byte-for-byte as it is.
No new dependency and no new file.

decisions.topic: How "fully inside" is judged for bound text in Wrap mode (assumption A-2)
decisions.choice: The label is copied with its computed position (`{ ...boundText, ...computeBoundTextPosition(container, boundText, elementsMap) }`, exactly as intersectionTest positions it) and its outline is `getElementLineSegments(positionedLabel, elementsMap)`; every point of those segments must be inside the lasso polygon and no lasso segment may intersect the positioned label.
rejected: elementsSegments.get(boundText.id): built from the label's stored x/y, which can lag its computed position, and the test helper builds it from the map including deleted elements
corners of getElementBounds(label): an axis-aligned box is larger than a rotated label, so rotated containers would be wrongly rejected
decisions.reason: Same outline function as A-1 and the same position the crossing test already uses, so enclosure and crossing judge one shape.

decisions.topic: Bound text elements as their own candidates in Wrap mode
decisions.choice: In "contain" mode an element for which isBoundToContainer(element) is true is never added to the result; it is judged only through its container (decision above). In "overlap" mode bound text is handled exactly as today.
rejected: judge bound text on its own in contain mode: a lasso around only the label would select it and selectElementsFromIds would promote it to the container, selecting a container that is not wrapped
decisions.reason: Matches rectangle box selection, which ignores bound text (shouldIgnoreElementFromSelection), and keeps FR-4: a container is selected only when both it and its label are wrapped.

decisions.topic: Where Wrap results go and what Overlap keeps
decisions.choice: The "overlap" branch keeps today's enclosureTest-then-intersectionTest code unchanged; the "contain" branch adds a wrapped element's id to enclosedElements and never touches intersectedElements; the returned array is still `[...intersectedElements, ...enclosedElements]`.
rejected: a third result set for wrapped elements: changes the function's state contract for no gain
decisions.reason: FR-2 and FR-6: Overlap is byte-for-byte today's algorithm and the result shape is unchanged.

decisions.topic: Building the lasso polygon and segments in Wrap mode
decisions.choice: Built once per call, before the element loop, from the simplified `path`, and only when mode is "contain" and `path.length > 0`; with an empty path Wrap selects nothing. Lasso segments are consecutive path points plus the closing segment last-to-first, produced by one shared helper getLassoSegments that intersectionTest also calls.
rejected: build per element as enclosureTest does: repeats work per candidate (NFR-3)
build unconditionally: polygonFromPoints on an empty path reads an undefined first point
decisions.reason: NFR-3 allows one build per call, and the shared helper keeps the two modes' notion of the lasso path identical.

decisions.topic: Default mode and where the live value is read
decisions.choice: getLassoSelectedElementIds destructures `boxSelectionMode = "overlap"`; LassoTrail.updateSelection passes `boxSelectionMode: this.app.state.boxSelectionMode` on every call; no caching of the mode in LassoTrail.
rejected: default "contain" to match the app default: would change the existing test helper's results (AC-1)
decisions.reason: FR-1 and FR-7: omitted input keeps today's behaviour and a preference change applies to the next lasso.

decisions.topic: How the new tests drive the lasso
decisions.choice: Mode tests drive the real lasso tool with a Pointer (`mouse.downAt`, `mouse.moveTo`, `mouse.up`) after `API.setAppState({ boxSelectionMode })`, on scenes built with API.createElement (roughness 0) and API.setElements; one test calls getLassoSelectedElementIds directly to pin the omitted/overlap/contain inputs. The existing updatePath helper and existing cases are not changed.
rejected: add a mode argument to updatePath: updatePath also runs the live LassoTrail, so it would not show which mode LassoTrail read
decisions.reason: AC-6 needs the real tool reading live state, and AC-1 keeps the existing cases untouched.

units.behaviour: getLassoSelectedElementIds takes an optional boxSelectionMode (default "overlap"); "overlap" runs today's enclosure-or-crossing algorithm unchanged, "contain" selects only elements whose whole outline (and whole positioned label) is inside the lasso polygon and not crossed by the lasso path.
rules: 1. Imports: add getElementLineSegments and isBoundToContainer to the existing `@excalidraw/element` import (names kept alphabetical); add LineSegment and Polygon to the existing `@excalidraw/math/types` type import; add a new last import `import type { AppState } from "../types";` separated by a blank line from the package type imports. No other import changes.

2. Input type gains `boxSelectionMode?: AppState["boxSelectionMode"];` after simplifyDistance; the destructuring gains `boxSelectionMode = "overlap",` after simplifyDistance. The return type and value stay `{ selectedElementIds: string[] }` built as `[...intersectedElements, ...enclosedElements]`.
3. Simplification, the unlockedElements filter, the two clear() calls and the lassoBounds reduce stay exactly as they are and in the same order.

4. After lassoBounds and before the element loop, build the Wrap inputs once: `const wrapLasso = boxSelectionMode === "contain" && path.length > 0 ? { polygon: polygonFromPoints(path), segments: getLassoSegments(path) } : null;` (from the simplified `path`).

5. The element loop keeps the same AABB pre-filter condition (doBoundsIntersect(lassoBounds, elementBounds) and not already in either set). Inside it: when boxSelectionMode === "contain", add element.id to enclosedElements only if `!isBoundToContainer(element) && wrapLasso && wrapTest(wrapLasso.polygon, wrapLasso.segments, element, elementsMap, elementsSegments)`; never add to intersectedElements in this branch. Otherwise (overlap) run today's code verbatim: enclosureTest, then intersectionTest only when not enclosed.

6. New module-private `const getLassoSegments = (lassoPath: GlobalPoint[]): LineSegment<GlobalPoint>[]` returns the consecutive segments `lineSegment(lassoPath[index], point)` over `lassoPath.slice(1)` followed by the closing segment `lineSegment(lassoPath[lassoPath.length - 1], lassoPath[0])`, exactly the expression intersectionTest uses today.
7. intersectionTest's `const lassoSegments = ...` expression becomes `const lassoSegments = getLassoSegments(lassoPath);`; the rest of intersectionTest and all of enclosureTest are unchanged.

8. New module-private `const isOutlineInside = (segments: LineSegment<GlobalPoint>[], lassoPolygon: Polygon<GlobalPoint>): boolean` returns false for an empty array, else true only when every point of every segment satisfies polygonIncludesPointNonZero(point, lassoPolygon).

9. New module-private `const isCrossedByLasso = (element: ExcalidrawElement, elementsMap: ElementsMap, lassoSegments: LineSegment<GlobalPoint>[]): boolean` returns true when some lasso segment gives `intersectElementWithLineSegment(element, elementsMap, lassoSegment, 0, true).length > 0`.

10. New module-private `const wrapTest = (lassoPolygon: Polygon<GlobalPoint>, lassoSegments: LineSegment<GlobalPoint>[], element: ExcalidrawElement, elementsMap: ElementsMap, elementsSegments: ElementsSegmentsMap): boolean`, evaluated in this order: (a) segments = elementsSegments.get(element.id); return false when undefined; (b) return false unless isOutlineInside(segments, lassoPolygon); (c) return false when isCrossedByLasso(element, elementsMap, lassoSegments); (d) boundTextElement = getBoundTextElement(element, elementsMap); when it is null return true; (e) positionedLabel = `{ ...boundTextElement, ...computeBoundTextPosition(element, boundTextElement, elementsMap) }`; return false unless isOutlineInside(getElementLineSegments(positionedLabel, elementsMap), lassoPolygon); (f) return !isCrossedByLasso(positionedLabel, elementsMap, lassoSegments).

11. The new helpers are appended after intersectionTest as `const` arrow functions; none is exported. Add no comments beyond one short line above wrapTest stating it implements the Wrap (contain) rule.

units.behaviour: Adds a describe block "Lasso respects boxSelectionMode" that drives the real lasso tool under "contain" and "overlap" plus one direct call pinning the default; existing helper and cases are untouched.
rules: 1. Imports: add `import { API } from "./helpers/api";` and `import { Keyboard, Pointer } from "./helpers/ui";` before the ./test-utils import, and change that import to `import { act, assertSelectedElements, render } from "./test-utils";`. No other import changes.

2. Append one top-level `describe("Lasso respects boxSelectionMode", () => { ... })` after the last existing describe. Inside it: `const mouse = new Pointer("mouse");` and a beforeEach that calls `mouse.reset()` and `act(() => h.app.setActiveTool({ type: "lasso" }))` (the file-level beforeEach already renders the editor).

3. A local helper `const lassoAround = (points: [number, number][], shift = false) => {...}` inside the describe: runs `mouse.downAt(points[0][0], points[0][1])`, `mouse.moveTo(x, y)` for each remaining point, `mouse.moveTo(points[0][0], points[0][1])` to close, then `mouse.up()`; when shift is true the whole sequence runs inside `Keyboard.withModifierKeys({ shift: true }, ...)`. Screen and scene coordinates coincide in the test editor (zoom 1, no scroll, zero offset).

4. Each case sets the mode with `API.setAppState({ boxSelectionMode: "contain" })` or `"overlap"` before drawing; never rely on the app default. Build scenes with API.createElement({ ..., roughness: 0 }) and API.setElements, keep every element and lasso point inside 0..900 on both axes, and assert with assertSelectedElements (assertSelectedElements() for an empty selection).

5. Lasso paths are polygons given by their corner points (4 for a rectangle); a "surrounding" lasso has a 40px margin around the element's AABB, a "partial" lasso covers only the element's left half with a 40px margin on the other three sides (for the 100x100 rectangle at 300,300: x 260..350, y 260..440), a "crossing" lasso is a 20px-high band through the element's middle extending 40px past both sides (x 260..440, y 340..360). The direct-call case passes the partial corners as `pointFrom<GlobalPoint>(x, y)` values.

6. Bound-text cases use `API.createTextContainer({ label: { text: "label" } })` (rectangle 0..100 at x=y=0 with a 50x20 label), then API.updateElement to move the rectangle to x 300, y 300 with width 300, height 100, and API.setElements([rectangle, text]); position the lasso relative to the label's computed position, which is horizontally left-aligned at the container's left padding (x 305) and vertically top-aligned (y 305) under the test defaults.

7. The direct-call case builds elementsSegments with getElementLineSegments for each h.elements entry (as updatePath does) and calls getLassoSelectedElementIds three times on the same partial lasso path: with boxSelectionMode omitted, with "overlap", with "contain"; it compares selectedElementIds arrays.
8. Do not modify updatePath, any existing describe, or the file header comment.
